title: Refit a car headrest at its lowest notch: both posts into their sleeves, then hold the release button and push it down
instruction: Put the headrest back into the seat, locked at its lowest position, then let go of it.
context: Fitting headrests into seat backs is a station on every car-seat and vehicle assembly line, and seats are refitted after repairs and recalls: it is the kind of fit-and-lock operation done all shift by team assemblers (BLS May 2024: 1,457,800 miscellaneous assemblers and fabricators, which include team assemblers). Both posts must go into both sleeves at once. The lock works the common way: a sprung pawl clicks into each notch and stops the headrest going down unless the release button is held in (raising is free). So one hand holds the button while the other lowers the headrest, then lets the button out so the pawl drops into the lowest notch.
setup: Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights are above the table top. Car seat back, top section (cropped 105 mm below the top, at the table), fixed to the table, facing the robot: charcoal upholstered block 100 mm thick (x 0.27 to 0.37) and 440 mm wide (y -0.22 to 0.22, its full width, shoulders squared), its top 77 mm up. Two guide sleeves on its top at x = 0.32, y = +/-0.10 (200 mm apart), vertical (a real seat back reclines them with it): black plastic bezels 28 x 28 mm standing 28 mm proud (tops 105 mm up), square bores 16 mm (1 mm play round a 14 mm post) widening to 26 mm over their top 6 mm, closed 96.5 mm below the bezels' tops. The right sleeve has the lock: a sprung latch whose pawl tooth (8 x 5 mm, centred 12 mm below the bezel's top) stands 4.5 mm into the bore from its inboard side; the grey release button (14 x 16 mm cap, 6 mm proud) sits on top of the bezel's outboard extension (a 20 mm wide housing reaching 48 mm outboard of the sleeve's axis), its centre 36 mm outboard of the axis. Pressing it down drives the latch through a 45-degree face; 5.8 mm down draws the pawl clear (the latch's spring 2 N at rest, 3.1 N drawn back; the button's 1.5 N). Headrest: charcoal fabric cushion 260 mm wide, 170 mm tall, 105 mm thick across its middle and 64 mm thick over its outer 32 mm at each end; two chromed steel posts, 14 mm, 200 mm apart, standing 130 mm out of its bottom; 1.0 kg. Each post has four notches 15 mm apart on its inboard face (8 mm tall, 3 mm deep; the first, nearest the tip, square; the others with a flat upper face and a 45-degree lower face) and a chamfered tip (inboard edge, 5.5 mm over 9.5 mm). The notches' depths (post tips below the bezels' tops with the pawl centred in the notch) are 50, 65, 80 and 95 mm; resting on the pawl the tips sit 1.5 mm deeper, and at 96.5 mm they also rest on the sleeves' closed ends. Start: the headrest leans back against the seat about 21 degrees, centred on y = 0, its post tips on the table 96 mm in front of the sleeves' axes, the lower back edge of its cushion resting on the two bezels' tops. Nothing else is on the table; the arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Measured in the seat's frame. 0 if at any time the headrest leaves the table (any corner of it more than 2 cm below the table top); is dropped (its centre falling faster than 0.5 m/s, a free fall of about 1.3 cm, while every part of both grippers is at least 2 cm from it; setting it down gently is fine); is forced more than 4 mm into the seat; or a post is forced past the pawl (more than 1.5 mm into it, or carried 1.5 mm past a notch's flat face between two control steps with the button out at both). Otherwise the stage at the end: 0.25 both post tips at least 20 mm down their sleeves (axes within 9 mm of the sleeves' axes); 0.5 the pawl engaged in a notch (button out, the pawl within 1.5 mm of its rest stop, the right post's tips within 2.5 mm of that notch's depth: 50, 65, 80 or 95 mm), posts within 6 degrees of the sleeves' axes; 0.75 locked at the lowest position: the pawl engaged in the lowest notch (tips 95 +/- 2.5 mm down) and the posts within 3 degrees of the sleeves' axes; 1.0 (success, held 1 s): locked at the lowest position, every part of both grippers at least 2 cm from the headrest, the headrest still (under 1 cm/s and 0.1 rad/s) and the lock still. Doing nothing or refusing scores 0.
reset_notes: Hold the release button down and lift the headrest out. Lean it back against the seat at its mark: post tips on the table 96 mm in front of the sleeves, centred, the lower back edge of the cushion on the two bezels.
fidelity: Rigid boxes; 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Headrest: one rigid body; cushion as three blocks (foam give plays no part), posts as boxes carrying notches, ramps and tip chamfers (14 mm square section; real posts are round and flex slightly). Seat: fixed-base articulation; latch and button on sprung prismatic joints (spring rates estimated), the button's stem pushing the latch's 45-degree face. Bores have 1 mm play each side (real guides are tighter). Sleeves vertical.
